output.entity_proposed: National Commission for the Filipino Family (NCFF)
output.proposal: HB No. 11572, the proposed "Filipino Family Mainstreaming Act," seeks to institutionalize a family mainstreaming framework, establish the National Commission for the Filipino Family (NCFF) as an inter-agency coordinating, advisory and monitoring body, and require Family Impact Assessments of major government policies, so that family considerations are systematically integrated into policymaking, planning and budgeting.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine whether the NCFF, chaired by the Executive Secretary with the DSWD as Secretariat, duplicates the coordinating mandates of existing bodies represented in it, such as the Council for the Welfare of Children, the Commission on Population and Development and the Philippine Commission on Women, and how its creation squares with the streamlining of the Executive branch and the reduction of overlapping functions under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231); Section 10 (Powers and Functions of the NCFF) and Section 35 (Non-Duplication of Government Functions) are relevant to this assessment. The review should also assess the workload that Family Impact Assessments, agency family mainstreaming plans and focal point systems would place on covered agencies and LGUs. The measure does not directly correspond to any FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority area and is not among the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda measures.
legislative_history: HB No. 11572 was filed in the House of Representatives on October 5, 2026, in the 20th Congress; its current status is filed (pending), with later stages not yet recorded.
HB No. 11832, also filed in the 20th Congress, likewise proposes a National Commission on the Filipino Family with a family welfare and development framework, but with a different design.
No earlier version of the measure from the 18th or 19th Congress was identified, and no Senate counterpart, substitute bill or committee report was identified.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11572 seeks to institutionalize the Filipino family mainstreaming framework and establish the National Commission for the Filipino Family (NCFF) as an inter-agency coordinating body. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 5 (Definition of Terms) provides definitions of family mainstreaming, the Family Impact Assessment, family well-being indicators, major government policy, the family mainstreaming focal point and the best interests of the family.
b. Section 8 (Composition of the National Commission for the Filipino Family) provides that the NCFF shall be chaired by the Executive Secretary, with thirteen department and agency heads, including the DBM, as members, together with representatives of local government leagues, civil society, the academe, faith-based organizations and the business sector, the private sector representatives serving on a voluntary, contributory and commitment basis.
c. Section 9 (Secretariat) provides that the Department of Social Welfare and Development shall serve as the NCFF Secretariat, using existing plantilla positions and organizational structures as far as practicable.
d. Section 10 (Powers and Functions of the NCFF) provides that the NCFF shall formulate the national family framework, recommend family policies, prescribe Family Impact Assessment standards, develop family well-being indicators, coordinate agency policies, monitor implementation and prepare an annual State of the Filipino Family Report, exercising primarily coordinating, advisory and monitoring functions without duplicating agency operations.
e. Section 20 (Family Welfare Disqualification in Government Procurement) provides that entities with a final decision or conviction for violating laws protecting life, women, children and family welfare shall not be awarded government procurement contracts.
f. Section 24 (Overseas Workers and Families Left Behind) provides that LGUs, through their social welfare and development offices, shall develop modules and interventions for families of overseas Filipino workers within the existing Parent Effectiveness Service Program, subject to available resources.
g. Section 27 (Family Mainstreaming in Budget Preparation) provides that covered agencies shall integrate family mainstreaming programs in their plans and budget proposals, that such programs may be charged to the GAD budget only when they meet GAD requirements, and that no mandatory earmarks or fixed expenditure percentages are required.
h. Section 39 (Appropriations) provides that initial implementation shall be charged against the current appropriations of the DSWD and participating agencies, with subsequent funding included in the annual General Appropriations Act.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 11572 may be considered alongside HB No. 11832, which proposes a similar National Commission on the Filipino Family but with the DSWD Secretary as Chairperson and a broader membership, and the two measures may be candidates for consolidation. The measure does not directly align with an FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework priority area or the LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda. The review should assess whether the NCFF duplicates the coordinating mandates of existing councils and commissions in light of the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231); whether attributing family programs to the GAD budget under Section 27 (Family Mainstreaming in Budget Preparation) is consistent with RA No. 9710; whether the procurement disqualification in Section 20 (Family Welfare Disqualification in Government Procurement) is consistent with RA No. 12009; and whether the LGU interventions in Section 24 (Overseas Workers and Families Left Behind) fit within the Parent Effectiveness Service Program under RA No. 11908.
